surface: Handrail HTML flyer camera and proposal notes
scope: Current redesign, published and browser-verified; no full global certification or user visual acceptance claim.

notes: No base salary, collection-based commissions,15/5 versus 20/5 and the 90-day proposal window match the business intent. Handrail prepares the final contract.
Current chapter, camera progress and Read normally / Take the tour labels expose the active presentation state.
The cash receipt explains money received before commission; retained funds explicitly exclude delivery, benefits and other costs.
Chapter buttons, a persisted reading preference, direct proposal notes and a matching PDF let readers bypass the camera journey.
The actual Handrail wordmark, warm paper/rust palette and locally served Inter/Playfair typography establish a coherent brand treatment.
Content is explicitly a proposal for discussion. No signature or acceptance mechanism exists; unagreed qualifying-client and benefits details remain discussion points.
Rates have explicit collected-fee labels; notes provide a linked seven-section table of contents.
Readers can select chapters, use ordinary scrolling or open the notes and PDF directly.
Root rendered review covered all six desktop stops. The actual branded flyer is the scene; the paperclip and separate 3D sculpture are removed.
No-JavaScript and system reduced-motion paths retain the complete proposal in ordinary document flow. No renderer or WebGL dependency remains.
Concise proposal notes explain the commercial structure, requested support and discussion points without legal boilerplate.
Reviewed desktop stops emphasize no base salary, collection timing and the two build rates.

19 browser tests passed. Camera framing checks at 320/390/1440 now assert rendered body text of at least 12px; ordinary reading reflows at 320/390/768/1440. Final cash-flow body text measured 12.2px at 320 and 14.9px at 390. Root reviewed the desktop/mobile captures.
Automated app and three component checks have zero axe violations. Manual VoiceOver and physical-device review remain unperformed.
Proposed status, commission timing, benefits cost and visible presentation controls are stated plainly.

Current local Lighthouse evidence records 100 in all categories on mobile/desktop and passing LCP, CLS and 250KB route-script budgets. It precedes the final keyboard/back-navigation cleanup; field INP and physical-device performance remain unmeasured.
No forms.
No text inputs or paste interception.
Keyboard chapter navigation, mode switching and skip-link activation are tested; an exhaustive focus-obscuration review is not claimed.
Emulated viewports do not establish physical notched-device coverage.
System reduced motion selects ordinary reading with no camera transform. A saved reading preference survives reload and motion-preference changes.
GSAP coordinates explicit translate, scale and rotation properties; reading mode removes the camera transform.
Desktop and mobile rendered review includes the final 320px typography polish; automated chapter checks verify framing and a 12px minimum rendered body size.
Rates and the illustrative payment arithmetic are checked; the 90-day window is a proposal term, not a live countdown.
No live date or locale-sensitive client rendering.
An emulated 390px touch gesture moves the flyer in browser QA. Physical-device interaction is unverified.
Both proposal PDF pages were visually reviewed with a balanced page break and white background. Independent text verification matched the introduction, seven sections, 15 paragraphs and endnote.
Rendered rate numerals retain associated percentage and collected-fee labels.
Native buttons and links, named navigation, headings and landmarks expose the camera and reading paths through the DOM.
Static app; no API, database, authentication or business mutation states.
